text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Lebanon is still on the U.S. list of countries that produce drugs, U.S. President Clinton says in a letter to Congress.
-The cabinet decided to extend the mandate of the current municipal councils, elected more than 30 years ago, until the beginning of June.
-General prosecuter Adoum dismisses reports that the health of imprisoned former Christian Maronite warlord Geagea is deteriorating, saying he is in good health.
-The Lebanese central bank's reserves excluding gold reserves and banks' deposits reach $4 billion, the Bank of Lebanon's governor Salameh said.
-Subscription in the treasury bills makes up 65 percent of commercial banks' revenues, Chairman of the Banks Association Bassil said.
-Casino du Liban, the biggest gambling and entertainment center in the Middle East before the 1975-90 civil war, opened its doors to the public yesterday.
-French contracts in Lebanon are estimated at eleven billion French francs.
-A Finnish business delegation met Lebanese officials and discussed the investment opportunities in Lebanon.
